Ivy: quick design spike — compact scorecard + approval affordances. Figma: https://figma.redwood/compact-scorecard-spike. Main issue: keyboard users can't find bulk actions when list collapses. Ravi: saw it. In compact rows the bulk checkbox and approve button are hidden behind a menu. Can we expose a lightweight action rail instead? Prefer minimal footprint + clear labels. Nora: copy idea for the rail: 'Approve visible results' and 'Re-run visible'. Include real counts when available, e.g. 'Approve 5 visible results'. Keep confirmation modal explicit: 'Approving will mark these results as expected for this prompt set. You can revert from regression history.' Sam: accessibility checklist: 1) action rail must remain in DOM order after the results list so Tab order is stable; 2) announce appearance with aria-live="polite" ("Actions available: Approve visible results, Re-run"); 3) don't move focus automatically; only focus when user triggers shortcut. Example snippet for PR: ```
``` QA Bot: e2e report: /e2e/prompt-evals/compact-action-rail.spec.js failing — test expects rail after list in DOM. Current impl injects at top, causing tab to jump. Ivy: proposal: render rail after list, absolutely position it to bottom:0. For keyboard discoverability add a skip link at top: 'Skip to actions (press Shift+\u002E)'. We'll document shortcut in help overlay. Ravi: analytics: log action_rail_shown with {visible_count, breakpoint}. When approve fired, include {approved_scope: "visible"|"all", approved_count}. Nora: small microcopy tweak: use 'Approve visible results' rather than generic 'Approve' to avoid ambiguity. Confirm CTA should be 'Approve 5 results' (dynamic). Secondary link 'View changes'. Cancel remains 'Cancel'. Sam: implement aria-hidden toggling: keep the rail in DOM but off-screen with aria-hidden=true until visible; when showing, remove aria-hidden, announce via aria-live, and if user used shortcut focus the first button. Avoid rapid toggles that confuse assistive tech. Ana: design note: add subtle divider line and 2px shadow so the rail reads as a separate surface. Token names in Figma: surface.divider.low, shadow.small-2. QA Bot: please update e2e to assert DOM order and tab sequence; current flaky failures on Chrome headless should be resolved with the DOM-order change. Ivy: action items: Ravi update Figma, Sam add aria snippets and keyboard behavior to PR, Nora finalize copy strings (i18n keys), Ana confirm visual tokens, QA to update tests. Sync Mon 9:30 to verify. Thanks! :thumbsup:
